items.title: Newly identified transport pathway reveals how caveolin-1 helps cells store fat
items.text: Lipodystrophy is a serious metabolic disease characterized by abnormal lipid storage in the body. In people with this condition, ingested fats are not stored in adipose tissue as they are in healthy individuals, but are instead deposited in the liver, muscle tissue or the heart muscle, among other places, with far-reaching metabolic consequences such as fatty liver or type 2 diabetes. The visible redistribution of fat in the body and the other symptoms are very distressing for patients. The causes of the disease may include a congenital gene mutation, an immune disorder or an infection.
